The BYM2 area structure

Source: R/sep.R
bym2sc.Rd

The scaled structure of the BYM2 model of Riebler et al. (2016): the generalised inverse G of the Laplacian Q of the neighbour weights (from its eigenvalues above tol times the largest), the scaling factor s, the geometric mean of the diagonal of G, so that the structured effect has a generalised variance of 1, and the covariance of the area effects ((1 - phi) I + phi G / s) / tau. The graph must be connected and every area must have a neighbour.

Usage

bym2sc(w, tau = 1, phi = 0.5, tol = 1e-10)

Arguments

w

The neighbours: spwt()'s list, an spdep listw or an n x n matrix of weights from 0 (its non-zero entries off the diagonal).

tau

The precision: one positive number.

phi

The share of the variance that is structured: one number from 0 to 1.

tol

The relative eigenvalue tolerance: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

A list: scale, ginv and cov.

References

Riebler, A., Sorbye, S. H., Simpson, D. and Rue, H. (2016). An intuitive Bayesian spatial model for disease mapping that accounts for scaling. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 25(4), 1145-1165. doi:10.1177/0962280216660421

See also

Other spatial epidemiology: bayout(), bufexp(), ecolrg(), evfilt(), kerexp(), lerprc(), sfrail(), spbias(), spsir()

Examples

w <- rbind(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(1, 0, 1, 0), c(1, 1, 0, 1), c(0, 0, 1, 0))
bym2sc(w, 2, 0.4)$scale
#> [1] 0.3565926
